cases.label: bug
cases.ground_truth: Known defect fixed by HTTPX PR #2998. With default unchunked text streaming, Response.iter_text passes the decoder flush result to TextChunker.decode. When that result is empty, this snapshot returns [content] even for content == "", so the iterator yields a spurious trailing empty string. Accept a finding that identifies this empty-text branch and its extra yielded chunk. Do not count ordinary empty response text, which is valid, or unrelated decoding claims.

cases.label: fixed
cases.ground_truth: Fixed snapshot for HTTPX PR #2998. TextChunker.decode returns [] when unchunked content is empty and preserves a list containing nonempty content. The upstream regression test expects iter_text over two byte chunks to yield only the two decoded strings, without a trailing empty string. Do not report the repaired empty-chunk issue as still present; other alleged defects need independent source evidence.

cases.label: bug
cases.ground_truth: Known defect fixed by attrs PR #1417. When field_transformer returns a generator, _transform_attrs assigns that one-shot generator to attrs. The mandatory/default order loop consumes it before the alias, name, and AttrsClass construction loops reuse it, so transformed fields can disappear from attrs.fields. Accept a finding that identifies the one-shot iterable reuse and lost fields. Do not count a transformer that returns a reusable list or tuple as this defect.

cases.label: fixed
cases.ground_truth: Fixed snapshot for attrs PR #1417. _transform_attrs materializes field_transformer output with tuple(...), allowing all later passes to inspect the same attributes. The upstream regression test uses a generator hook and checks that attrs.fields retains x. Do not claim the earlier one-shot exhaustion remains; any different claim needs source-backed review.

cases.label: bug
cases.ground_truth: Known asyncio CapacityLimiter cancellation defect from AnyIO issue #947, repaired in PR #952. When release_on_behalf_of pops and signals the first waiter, cancellation can reach that waiter before it adds itself to _borrowers. This snapshot only removes it from _wait_queue and re-raises; because the signaled waiter has already been popped, the next queued waiter is never notified despite free capacity. Accept a finding that identifies the lost wake-up and waiting-task hang under this cancellation interleaving. Do not count normal cancellation cleanup without the already-signaled waiter as this defect.

cases.label: fixed
cases.ground_truth: Fixed snapshot for AnyIO issue #947. The cancellation handler checks whether the current event was already signaled and, if so, calls _notify_next_waiter; release_on_behalf_of uses the same helper. The upstream regression test starts two waiting borrowers, cancels the first, and requires the second to acquire. Do not claim this lost wake-up persists; other concurrency claims require independent evidence.
